correctness.rationale: The parity of common goods before the first private good gives an unavoidable integer lower bound on every prefix. Explicit allocation makes the signed common imbalance X in {-1,0} when agent 1 receives the first private good or {0,1} when agent 2 does, so E=max(0,-A-X,X-B) equals the lower bound before that arrival and zero thereafter. The indistinguishable-common-first two-input family has offline optimum 1, costs at least m on the wrong initial assignment regardless of subsequent decisions, and a uniform first coin matches the (m+1)/2 randomized minmax. Exhaustive independent state-based DP for all 87381 valuation profiles through m=8 corroborates but does not prove generality.

value.rationale: The first fully specified tractable heterogeneous binary case of the cumulative maximum envy optimization from [1] obtains an explicit exact formula, stronger simultaneous optimization of every prefix, and a striking exact two-instance separation between clairvoyant and no-future-information allocation. The improvement is structural rather than a mere small input case or arbitrary enumeration and directly informs whether lookahead matters in fairness-over-time mechanisms.
